newsitem.title: USA: U.S. space shuttle Discovery lands in Florida.
newsitem.headline: U.S. space shuttle Discovery lands in Florida.

text.p: The space shuttle Discovery landed in Florida on Tuesday with a satellite carrying a bounty of data about the health of Earth's protective ozone layer.
The $2 billion gliding spaceship set down at 7:08 a.m. EDT (1108 GMT) on its landing strip at the Kennedy Space Center, one day late because of the weather.
Cradled in the shuttle's cargo bay was an ozone-monitoring satellite, holding enough atmospheric data to fill a half-ton of computer floppy disks.
The German-built spacecraft flew free of the shuttle for nine days and took nearly 50,000 atmospheric measurements to aid scientists studying the depletion of the ozone layer.
The satellite also provided evidence to support a controversial theory that the Earth is being bombarded daily by thousands of house-sized, water-laden comets.

During their 12-day flight, Discovery's crew of six also tested a Japanese prototype robot arm for the planned international space station and pointed a telescope at Comet Hale-Bopp as it raced away from the sun.
